From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@scalemate.com>

Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 09:05:12 -0400
Subject: EastUS - increased latency and 5xx rate (urgent)

Jordan —

We're seeing a sudden spike in p95/p99 latency for generation endpoints in EastUS starting ~08:55 ET and a correlated 5xx rate increase across the account (ScaleMate). Users are reporting retries and partial failures. Dashboard and initial logs attached.

Key details:
- Region: EastUS (primary AZ1)
- Latency: p99 from ~220ms -> 1.8s on text-gen routes
- Error rate: 0.6% -> 6% 5xx over the last 10m
- Throughput: throughput steady but tail latency rising

We are in production for onboarding several enterprise customers right now; this is impacting revenue-critical flows. Please escalate and advise immediate mitigation steps.

Attached: eastus_logs_0909.zip (snippet), metrics_screenshot.png

Thanks,
Maria Lopez
Ops Lead, ScaleMate

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 09:15:27 -04:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: EastUS - increased latency and 5xx rate (urgent)

Quick triage from infra side — evidence points to degraded NIC performance on a subset of instances in EastUS-A (AZ1). Packet drops are causing TCP retransmits and amplified p99 for real-time generation. Also seeing KV cache thrash on the local LRU shards which spikes CPU on a hot subset of hosts.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (short horizon):
1) Traffic evacuation: shift 30-40% of production traffic off EastUS to WestUS2 as an emergency measure (no model change).
   - Command: rwdctl route adjust --from-region eastus --to-region westus2 --fraction 0.35 --model-group gen-v2
2) Bump retry budget and reduce client-side timeout to avoid request storms while evacuation completes.
3) Drain suspect hosts in AZ1 and trigger instance replacement.

I'll coordinate with Sean on KV cache warming policy for the target region to reduce cold-start amplification. Evelyn, please follow the evacuation steps in the runbook and report progress every 5m.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Director, Infra Reliability
Redwood Inference

- What is cross-region capacity headroom for gen-v2 in WestUS2? Evelyn, the attached metrics snapshot shows current utilization.

I'm drafting a short exec blurb for Aditya/VPs: impact (customers affected, p99 increase, 5xx delta), mitigation (evacuation fraction, host replacement), and next steps (postmortem, quota adjustments). Will circulate in 10m.

Action update: initiated traffic evacuation at 09:37 ET. Current state: shifted 40% of gen-v2 traffic to WestUS2 using emergency routing policy; KV cache pre-warming started; draining 6 suspect hosts in EastUS-A.

Observability:
- p99 in EastUS trending down from 1.8s -> 420ms (so far)
- WestUS2 p99 increased modestly from 190ms -> 270ms but well within SLOs
- 5xx rate in EastUS decreased from 6% -> 1.1% after drain/evacuation

I've also opened a cloud provider ticket for the NIC anomalies and engaged them (cloudops@publiccloud.example). Will continue to monitor and will provide a 30m update.

Maria —

Thanks for the quick heads up and patience. Short summary of what we did and next steps:

What we observed:
- Rapid p99 increase and a correlated 5xx spike in EastUS (AZ1).

Immediate actions taken (09:37–09:42 ET):
- Emergency traffic evacuation: 40% of gen-v2 traffic shifted to WestUS2.
- Drained 6 suspect hosts in EastUS-A; KV pre-warming in target region.
- Opened cloud provider support ticket for NIC anomalies.

Customer impact now: reduced error rate and improved p99. We are monitoring for secondary effects (cache cold starts, capacity pressure) and will hold a postmortem tomorrow at 15:00 ET to review root cause and mitigation (invite to follow).

If you need a dedicated phone bridge for execs, I can set that up. We're treating this as a Sev2 with exec visibility and will follow up with the postmortem and any customer credits if appropriate.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll share the incident timeline and a remediation plan in the follow-up.

Best,
